correctness.rationale: The reciprocal quartic Q(t) reduces to a quadratic in t+t^-1, proving squarefreeness on exactly U. Two commuting involutions yield smooth genus-two quotients D and E related by reciprocal inversion. Their pullbacks yield a degree prime to five isogeny J(D)²→J(X), identifying p-divisible groups and ordinarity. For D, f(t)=(t+1)Q(t) has Cartier/Hasse-Witt matrix [[-2uv+2u+1,-2(u-v)(2u+1)],[-2uv,u²+4uv+2v]], whose determinant over F5 is Phi. Since d(u)=u²+2u-2 is coprime to n(u)=u²(2u+1), the divisor graph v=n/d has exactly four F5 punctures u=0,1,2,3 and two roots of d (irreducible discriminant 2). The derivative in v never vanishes there. Counting forbidden v=0,-u²,-1-u gives q²-3q+3 smooth parameter pairs, and puncture Frobenius orbits give q-4-2[2|m]. For (-1,2), the genus-two Hasse matrix [[3,4],[4,2]] has rank one and square zero; genus-two p-rank zero implies supersingular Newton polygon and a-number one, doubled by the isogeny. Independently verified determinant identities, geometric substitution, and direct complete F5 count: 13 smooth, 1 nonordinary (4,2). Finite extension-field scripts were inspected; finite checks corroborate but do not replace uniform arguments.
